summary: Built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3, Alpine 3.23) from scratch, seeded application data (appdb.orders), then added node4 as a fourth member that received a full SST of existing data and now accepts writes like the others. Diagnosed and fixed an Alpine-specific bug where BusyBox's ps/lsof lack flags the wsrep_sst_rsync script depends on (causing false "SST daemon terminated unexpectedly" / infinite-loop failures) by installing the procps and lsof packages on all nodes. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id and cluster-health baselines, restarted each of the 4 nodes one at a time via native reboot (quorum preserved throughout since only one node was ever down), confirmed each node came back with a new boot_id, and verified MariaDB auto-started (rc-update default runlevel), rejoined the Galera cluster (wsrep_cluster_size=4, status=Primary, local_state=Synced), and retained/replicated all application data after every restart.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb, mariadb-client, galera, rsync, procps, lsof via apk on node1-node4
Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS on all 4 nodes

Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf per node with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3,node4, wsrep_node_address, port=3306; disabled the conflicting skip-networking default in mariadb-server.cnf
Initialized MariaDB data directories (mariadb-install-db) on node1-node4
Bootstrapped the Galera cluster on node1 (wsrep-new-cluster), created appdb.orders with sample rows
Joined node2 and node3 to the cluster via rc-service (rsync SST), fixing the BusyBox ps/lsof incompatibility that was blocking SST
Reconciled node1 into normal OpenRC-managed lifecycle (stopped the manual bootstrap process, restarted via rc-service as a normal joiner once quorum existed)
Added node4 as a fourth cluster member: initialized its data dir, started mariadb, it performed SST and joined as wsrep_cluster_size=4
Verified multi-master writes: inserted rows on node3 and node4, confirmed near-instant visibility on other nodes
Added init.d start_pre() mkdir/chown for /run/mysqld and rc-update add mariadb default on all 4 nodes for boot persistence
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id + wsrep status + row data) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node4, node3, node2, node1 sequentially via native reboot, one at a time, polling until each came back, confirming new boot_id and full cluster/data recovery before proceeding to the next node
Performed a final post-all-restarts write/read consistency check across nodes
